Both Codex and ChatGPT Work fail with `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`, although regular Chat works. Event 2000 reports sandbox provisioning successful. Subsequent sandbox setup logs show `runtime read/execute validation failed` on `VCRUNTIME140_1.dll` in the bundled `cua_node` runtime, with `os error 32` (file in use). ProcMon observed a `CreateFile` sharing violation. During setup, `codex-computer-use-swift.exe` is already running as a child of `ChatGPT.exe` and has loaded this DLL. The issue persists after restarts, clean reinstalls, regenerating the runtime and fresh user configuration. Another workstation with the same Windows build, app version, runtime identifier and elevated sandbox setting works. Please investigate concurrent runtime loading versus sandbox ACL validation and advise a supported fix. Related: #52036, #52127.

## Summary
On October 8, Codex Desktop on Windows repeatedly failed to start browser control before it could read Chrome tabs. Sandbox setup failed on the bundled node_repl.exe with Windows error 32 during an ACL update. Ordinary sandbox shell commands were also affected.

## Affected environment
- Desktop version: 26.1002.52244, build 13536, production channel (verified by app update checker).
- Installed package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0 (verified locally).
- Update checker on October 8: up_to_date.
- Runtime: cua_node/3dd31cfff853001c/bin/node_repl.exe.
- Requested browser: signed-in Chrome. Failure occurred before browser access; Chrome was not established as the cause.

## Reproduction during the failure
1. Request browser inventory through cua.getState().
2. Runtime exits with node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly / trusted Node process exited unexpectedly.
3. Fresh diagnostics report windows sandbox failed: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors.
4. Reset the tool kernel, fully quit/reopen Codex, and reboot Windows.
5. Retry: same error. Latest verified post-reboot failure log time: 2026-10-08T19:31:22Z.

## Sanitized diagnostic excerpt

runtime read/execute validation failed:
validate runtime read/execute access on
%LOCALAPPDATA%/OpenAI/Codex/runtimes/cua_node/3dd31cfff853001c/bin/node_repl.exe:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
setup error: setup refresh had errors

## Observations
- Helpers using the executable were started after the reboot and had Codex or its bundled Node process as parent; they were not established as pre-reboot orphan processes.
- Ordinary sandbox shell execution failed; approved host shell diagnostics worked.
- A scheduled local stats refresh at 08:58–09:02 America/Chicago completed, but its first ordinary command failed with the same setup error before a retry succeeded. It used Python/local commands and did not test browser control.
- During the initial diagnosis, no binaries, ACLs, or sandbox settings were changed by this reporting chat. No credentials, private project data, or full session logs are attached.

## Recovery follow-up
Later on October 8, browser inventory, reading an existing GitHub tab, and opening this issue form succeeded. Ordinary shell reading also succeeded. The current session therefore has recovered access. The exact intervening environment change and the cause of recovery have not yet been verified by this reporting chat; this report preserves the earlier reproducible failure rather than claiming it is still occurring now.

## Expected behavior and impact
Browser control and ordinary sandbox commands should start while Codex's own trusted helpers are running. The earlier failure blocked authenticated research for a time-sensitive sponsor exposure report despite resets, restarts, and a reboot.

## Related fix and request
https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/51822 was merged October 7 and appears relevant. Related report: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52033.
Please identify the first Windows desktop release containing #51822 and a supported recovery procedure that preserves sandbox protections, chats, and browser sessions. Inclusion of the fix in the affected installation was not verified.

**Closed as a duplicate of #51737.** Its [October 8 update](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51737#issuecomment-6063919778) already covers the same saved-environment Library-transfer HTTP 403 with successful authenticated browser downloads. This report retains additional reproduction details and a feedback ID. The attachment-materialization observations also overlap with #51576; a shared root cause is unconfirmed.

---

### What issue are you seeing?

In a Codex Cloud task launched from a saved cloud environment, I cannot get a small ZIP from my ChatGPT Library into the task's filesystem.

Two access paths fail:
1. The supported Library materialization flow accepts the file reference and reports its metadata, but the transfer helper exits with code 1:
   `library file transfer failed: download failed with HTTP status 403`
2. Both **Add from library** and a fresh browser **Upload** attach the file to the conversation, but the task sees only a `sediment://...` reference. It reports that the file is not present locally and that it has no available tool to obtain the attachment's bytes. Asking explicitly to save it under `/workspace` does not produce the file.

The same 515,044-byte ZIP downloads successfully from Library in my browser. No readable local ZIP was obtained in the cloud task, so its SHA-256 and CRC could not be checked there.

Related open reports found before filing:
- #51737, including [the comment reporting the same Library HTTP 403](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51737#issuecomment-6063919778)
- #51576, concerning attachment materialization in Cloud Work

This may be another instance of those reports. I am providing the combined observations and a feedback reference; please consolidate if appropriate.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

These steps reproduced the problem in my account on October 8, 2026:

1. Create/publish a saved cloud environment associated with a private GitHub repository.
2. Enable internet access, publish the updated configuration, and start a **new task** from that configuration. The new published environment version was confirmed before the new task was created.
3. Ask the task to materialize the small Library ZIP using the supported Library flow.
4. Observe the transfer-helper error above and absence of usable local file bytes.
5. As a separate test, attach the ZIP with **Add from library**, then ask the task to save and verify it under `/workspace`.
6. Separately download that ZIP in the browser and attach it using **Upload**, again explicitly asking the task to save it under `/workspace`.
7. In both attachment tests, the task receives a reference but reports no local file or available attachment-byte retrieval tool. This is a failure before opening or unzipping the file, not an `unzip` error.

### What is the expected behavior?

An authorized Library file or uploaded attachment should become readable in the task's workspace through a supported mechanism, allowing ordinary size, SHA-256 and ZIP-integrity checks without executing its contents.

### Additional information

- Client: ChatGPT web on Windows; execution occurs in the cloud task.
- Exact client/agent build and cloud OS version were not captured.
- Latest authorized Library reproduction: **2026-10-08 23:16:23 UTC**.
- Destination hostname for that failed request: `sdmntprbrazilsouth.oaiusercontent.com`.
- An earlier reproduction at **2026-10-08 21:11:00 UTC** failed with the same HTTP 403.
- The local execution environment was available, with approximately 30 GiB free when checked.

A bounded HTTPS HEAD diagnostic at **2026-10-08 21:06:08 UTC**, using the existing proxy and certificate configuration, returned:
- `pypi.org`: proxy CONNECT 200; final HTTP 200; curl exit 0.
- `sdmntprwestus.oaiusercontent.com`: proxy CONNECT 200; final HTTP 400; curl exit 0.
- `sdmntprbrazilsouth.oaiusercontent.com`: proxy CONNECT 200; final HTTP 400; curl exit 0.

These requests were to public host roots, not signed file URLs. They demonstrate responses from those roots but **do not establish that a specific file transfer is authorized or identify the cause of the 403**. I cannot determine whether this is a transfer-authorization, materialization, policy, or other service problem.

Support has escalated the case to a specialist. I submitted in-product feedback; the confirmation dialog explicitly labels **01a11d4c-bab5-71d5-ae17-2bb09c077039** as the **Feedback ID** (it also matches the task ID).

No signed URLs, credentials, private repository contents, or source files are included in this public report.

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, Codex Desktop recognizes and initializes an enabled custom stdio MCP server (`vibe-monitor`), and its logs report a successfully built MCP tool catalog with **6 available servers, 0 unavailable, and 886 total tools**. Nevertheless, the server's tools (`vibe_version` and `vibe_session_start`) are not callable from a Codex Desktop chat/task.

**On the same machine, an independent invocation of the Codex CLI using the same `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml` successfully invokes both tools.** This suggests a Desktop task tool-exposure / tool-injection issue after successful MCP initialization, rather than a broken MCP executable.

Possibly related to / duplicate of #51920 and #34018. This report adds concrete `logs_2.sqlite` connection-manager evidence and a same-machine CLI control test.

## Environment

- OS: Windows x64, `10.0.19041` (Windows 10)
- Codex Desktop: `OpenAI.Codex` MSIX package **`26.1002.7124.0`**, status `Ok` (`Get-AppxPackage -Name OpenAI.Codex`)
- Codex binary bundled with Desktop: **`0.162.0-alpha.2`** (reported by `codex.exe exec`)
- Server: `vibe-monitor` custom stdio MCP
- MCP runtime: bundled Node.js **`22.23.3`**, Windows x64
- Server software: **Vibe Monitor `0.3.0-beta.26`**
- User-level configuration: `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml`

Sanitized relevant config:

```toml
mcp_optional_startup_grace_ms = 0

[mcp_servers.vibe-monitor]
enabled = true
startup_timeout_sec = 30
command = "C:\\Users\\<USER>\\.vibe-monitor\\bin\\vibe-monitor.cmd"
args = ["mcp", "--agent", "codex"]

[mcp_servers.vibe-monitor.tools.vibe_version]
approval_mode = "approve"

[mcp_servers.vibe-monitor.tools.vibe_session_start]
approval_mode = "approve"
```

The initial issue reproduced prior to adding the startup grace and 30-second timeout options; adding them did **not** restore the missing Desktop tools.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register and enable `vibe-monitor` as a stdio MCP server in the user Codex config.
2. Confirm that `codex.exe mcp get vibe-monitor` reports:
   ```text
   enabled: true
   transport: stdio
   command: C:\Users\<USER>\.vibe-monitor\bin\vibe-monitor.cmd
   args: mcp --agent codex
   startup_timeout_sec: 30
   ```
3. Start Codex Desktop and open a Desktop chat/task. Inspect `/mcp` and request `vibe_version` or `vibe_session_start`. The tools are not available to the task, despite an MCP process having been launched.
4. Check Desktop's `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\logs_2.sqlite` read-only: see the successful initialization and catalog messages below.
5. As a control, invoke the Codex binary independently in a read-only sandbox:
   ```cmd
   "<PATH_TO_CODEX_EXE>\codex.exe" exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -C "<TEST_REPO>" "Actually call the vibe-monitor MCP tool vibe_version and report its result; do not edit files."
   ```
6. Observe that this independent CLI run successfully calls both `vibe-monitor/vibe_session_start` and `vibe-monitor/vibe_version`, with the latter returning `0.3.0-beta.26`.

## Actual behavior

- Desktop chat/task has no usable Vibe Monitor MCP tools.
- The stdio server is **enabled** in the effective CLI config; both launcher and runtime files exist.
- Desktop's MCP client initializes the server and the aggregate connection-manager catalog reports **no unavailable MCP servers**.
- Running the same configured MCP from the independent CLI succeeds.

## Expected behavior

A successfully initialized, enabled custom stdio MCP server's callable tools should be exposed to new Codex Desktop tasks. If a specific tool is excluded by a tool-budget/filtering/approval policy, Desktop should make that reason discoverable, rather than silently leaving the tool unavailable.

## Evidence from Desktop diagnostics

Read-only query of `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\logs_2.sqlite`:

```text
[4509] INFO rmcp::service
new{server_name=vibe-monitor}:start_server_task{server_name=vibe-monitor}:serve_inner:
Service initialized as client peer_info=Some(ServerPeerInfo {
  protocol_version: ProtocolVersion("2025-06-18"),
  capabilities: ... tools: Some(...)
})

[4510] TRACE codex_mcp::connection_manager::tool_catalog
list_tools_with_errors{mcp_server_count=6}:
built MCP tool list available_server_count=6 unavailable_server_count=0 tool_count=886

[4517] INFO rmcp::service
new{server_name=vibe-monitor}:start_server_task{server_name=vibe-monitor}:serve_inner:
task cancelled

[4521] INFO rmcp::service
new{server_name=vibe-monitor}:start_server_task{server_name=vibe-monitor}:serve_inner:
serve finished quit_reason=Cancelled
```

Notes on interpreting these logs:

- `tool_count=886` is the **aggregate** tool count across all available servers; it does not independently prove that every Vibe Monitor tool was admitted to this particular Desktop task.
- The `Cancelled` shutdown messages occurred for multiple servers (`node_repl`, `cua_repl`, `codex_app`, etc.) in the same block, not just Vibe Monitor, so they **do not establish** a Vibe Monitor-specific crash.
- A filtered query for recent `WARN`/`ERROR` logs and `codex_mcp::connection_manager::tool_catalog` records produced only the successful catalog line above.

## Independent CLI control — works

```text
OpenAI Codex v0.162.0-alpha.2
sandbox: read-only

mcp: vibe-monitor/vibe_session_start started
mcp: vibe-monitor/vibe_session_start (completed)
mcp: vibe-monitor/vibe_version started
mcp: vibe-monitor/vibe_version (completed)

Vibe Monitor version: 0.3.0-beta.26
```

Independent telemetry confirms a fresh `codex` invocation ran the actual compiled `0.3.0-beta.26` client (rather than only reading an installer version pointer), completed a full scan in 16 ms, and successfully reported the result to the server.

## Request

Could the Codex maintainers investigate the gap between **MCP initialization / aggregate tool-catalog creation** and the **tools actually injected into a new Windows Desktop task** in package `26.1002.7124.0` / runtime `0.162.0-alpha.2`?

Is `tool_count=886` expected to trigger a tool-selection limit, deferred-loading path, or per-task filtering that can silently omit tools from an otherwise healthy server?

No credentials, personal paths, session identifiers, device identifiers, or database contents are included in this report.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Not captured for the affected remote host. The reporter calls the desktop application “DSH Desktop”; its exact distribution, build, and relationship to the current Codex/ChatGPT desktop app have not been verified. Please treat this as a triage report, not a confirmed reproduction on a specific official build.

### What subscription do you have?

Not captured for the affected session.

### What platform is your computer?

The affected task is on a remote host, according to the reporter. Remote OS, architecture, execution backend, model, transport, and client version are unknown. The reporting computer's environment has deliberately not been substituted for the affected environment.

### What issue are you seeing?

A user reports that while the desktop UI is waiting in `wait_agent`, sending a follow-up question does not produce a reply. A supplied screenshot shows these items together:

- Tool status: `正在调用工具 · wait_agent` (Calling tool · wait_agent).
- A user message in the chat transcript: `还差多少` (How much is left?).
- Continuing activity status: `深度求索中，用时 10分47秒 …` (Working/thinking, elapsed 10m47s).
- No assistant reply below that follow-up in the captured viewport.

The elapsed 10m47s is the overall activity timer. It is NOT evidence that the follow-up itself waited that long, or that one wait_agent call lasted that long. The screenshot establishes the visible UI state, not server-side delivery, consumption, or message loss. No remote logs or deterministic reproduction are available yet.

The main concern is that the user cannot tell whether the new message is waiting for the next turn, has been accepted as steering but is pending, or is blocked behind an agent wait.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Reported sequence; not independently reproduced:

1. Run a task that delegates work to subagents on the affected remote host.
2. Observe the parent UI displaying an active `wait_agent` call.
3. Send a simple status question such as “How much is left?”.
4. Observe the question displayed in the chat while the agent continues to show an active wait and does not visibly reply, as reported by the user.

The selected follow-up mode (Steer versus Queue), actual time between sending and capture, wait timeout, session identifiers, and eventual recovery behavior have not been captured. The screenshot is insufficient to rule out intentional Queue behavior or a normal brief delay at a tool boundary.

Suggested investigation/reproduction matrix:

- Explicit Steer versus explicit Queue during a hosted agent wait.
- Local versus remote execution.
- Subagent notification versus wait timeout versus a new user input as the wake-up event.
- Follow-up acceptance, task-side consumption, and UI update timing measured separately.

### What is the expected behavior?

For Queue, clearly show that the question will be processed in the next run. For Steer, process it at the supported interruption boundary and expose a pending state if processing must be delayed. A prolonged wait should not silently make accepted follow-ups appear ignored.

The currently exposed collaboration.wait_agent tool description in the reporting session says that a wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. This is a runtime contract observed in the reporting session, not proof that the affected remote host uses the same version or implementation.

Official user guidance distinguishes Steer (current run) from Queue (next run):
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/prompting

The API steering guide also notes that acceptance is not consumption and that running tool work can delay continuation:
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/steering

Please clarify whether this visible state is expected for hosted `wait_agent`, and investigate wake-up/input delivery if explicit steering can remain unprocessed until subagent completion or the full wait timeout.

### Additional information

Reported on October 9, 2026 (Asia/Shanghai). This is a suspected responsiveness/state-visibility issue, not an established deadlock or confirmed root cause in the official desktop app.

Related issues checked before filing:

- #47762: steering before a wait can leave subagent results uncollected; different ordering from this report.
- #24951: agent waits and spawns can stall well beyond requested timeouts; this report has no timing logs to establish that mechanism.
- #51610: accepted follow-ups accumulate behind a long tool stall; involves another tool and has stronger delivery evidence than this report.

No exact duplicate was established from those reports. No shared cause is claimed. Raw screenshots, project text, filesystem paths, host addresses, account information, session identifiers, and credentials are omitted from this public report.

### What issue are you seeing?

The interactive Codex CLI panicked and exited to the shell while handling a Chinese question containing emoji. The terminal retained this error:

```text
The application panicked (crashed).
Message: end byte index 159 is not a char boundary; it is inside '➡' (bytes 158..161) of [application text omitted for privacy]
Location: tui/src/terminal_hyperlinks.rs:392

Backtrace omitted. Run with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 environment variable to display it.
Run with RUST_BACKTRACE=full to include source snippets.
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is an observed crash, not yet a deterministic end-to-end reproducer. The exact terminal dimensions and triggering UI action were not captured, and a full backtrace is unavailable.

1. Run `codex` version 0.162.0 in Kitty.
2. The affected interaction contains a long Chinese question, including `➡️` (business text omitted).
3. The TUI exits with the panic above during source-range remapping.

The application's business text has been omitted for privacy. The original panic identifies `➡` at UTF-8 bytes 158..161; offset 159 is inside that character.

### What is the expected behavior?

Rendering/wrapping Chinese text and emoji should not terminate the CLI. Source ranges used for slicing should remain valid UTF-8 boundaries and correctly map to the displayed text.

### Additional information

The reported location matches the code in the 0.162.0 tag:
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0/codex-rs/tui/src/terminal_hyperlinks.rs#L392

Inside `remap_source_wrapped_line`:

```rust
source_column += display_width(&text[source_byte..wrapped.range.start]);
```

The panic indicates that the range start used here was inside a multibyte character. The upstream cause of the invalid wrapped range still needs investigation; this report does not establish that the arrow alone always triggers a crash.

Related change: #52330 (commit 22ebb0fb178fe369190123c256ba200585765725) clamps wrapped range offsets to `text.len()` to address a cursor sentinel past the end of the input. That particular clamp does not address this case: 159 is already below the input length but is not a character boundary. A local Python byte-boundary check using the reported text confirmed that `min(159, len(text.encode("utf-8")))` remains 159 and the prefix still fails UTF-8 decoding. This was a boundary check only, not a Rust/TUI regression test.

Suggested investigation/regression coverage: exercise source-range remapping of long CJK questions with emoji/variation selectors across different wrap widths, and check both in-bounds character boundaries and preservation of visible text/source mappings.

### Bug

Japanese text is readable in the Codex desktop input composer. After submitting a message containing Markdown inline code and code blocks, Japanese inside those code sections appears as **small boxes containing question marks in the sent user-message bubble**.

The same rendering problem occurs in assistant response code sections. An assistant response is not needed to reproduce the sent user-message symptom.

### Expected vs. actual

| Location | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input composer before sending | 日本語テスト | 日本語テスト (correct) |
| Sent user message: inline code / regular code text | 日本語テスト | ⍰⍰⍰⍰⍰⍰ |
| Assistant response: inline code / regular code text | 日本語テスト | ⍰⍰⍰⍰⍰⍰ |
| Ordinary prose | 日本語テスト | 日本語テスト (correct) |
| Italic JavaScript comments in code | 日本語テスト | 日本語テスト (correct) |

⍰ is a visual approximation of the outlined boxes containing question marks shown on screen, not a claim about the literal characters in the underlying message. ASCII characters and syntax colors display correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Copy the sample below.
2. Paste it into the Codex desktop input composer. Japanese is readable at this stage.
3. Press Send.
4. Inspect your own sent message bubble. Japanese in inline code, the plain code block, JavaScript identifiers/string literals, and JSON keys/values appears as boxed question marks. The italic JavaScript comment and ordinary prose remain readable.
5. If Codex echoes the sample, the assistant response's code sections exhibit the same issue.

Japanese should remain readable after submitting the message and rendering its Markdown code sections, in both user messages and assistant responses.

- Desktop app: 26.1007.21159 (build 20052)
- Interface: Codex desktop chat
- OS: macOS 27.0 (26A428)
- Architecture: Apple Silicon

The input composer and the sent user-message bubble were compared in a screenshot: the composer displays the Japanese source normally, while the sent message's regular code text shows boxed question marks. # Codex CLI on Windows: elevated sandbox "setup refresh had errors" (os error 32) after update to 0.162.0-alpha.2

## Environment
- Windows 10 Enterprise 10.0.19045, x64.
- Codex desktop app package OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.7124.0_x64 (Microsoft Store / WindowsApps).
- Codex CLI `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2` at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\9691020b546a15b2\codex.exe`
  (auto-updated on 2026-10-08 ~11:40 local; the previous bin folder `2ffcf3015ebd52b4` was removed).
- `~/.codex/config.toml`: `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`.

## Symptom
All tested `codex exec -s workspace-write` runs in a trusted git worktree failed to execute tools:
```
Failed to create unified exec process: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
windows sandbox failed: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```
File writes via apply_patch also fail. The agent itself starts and reasons normally.

## Sandbox log (`~/.codex/.sandbox/sandbox.2026-10-09.log`)
```
setup refresh: spawning ...\bin\9691020b546a15b2\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe (cwd=..., payload_len=...)
runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on
  C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe:
  open ACL target for root-only update: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
setup refresh completed with errors: [...]
setup error: setup refresh had errors
codex.exe] setup refresh: exited with status ExitStatus(ExitStatus(1))
```
Decoded setup payload: `mode = "read-acls-only"`, `refresh_only = true`, `real_user = <machine>\<user>`, sandbox users
`CodexSandboxOffline` / `CodexSandboxOnline`. First failure in the log: 2026-10-08 20:07 local (after the update).

## What was checked
- ACLs on `node_repl.exe` and all parent folders already grant `CodexSandboxUsers:(RX)` (inherited); owner is the real user.
- At rest the file is not locked: an exclusive open succeeds; as the non-elevated real user, opening with READ_CONTROL|WRITE_DAC
  (and WRITE_OWNER) succeeds; only GENERIC_WRITE fails with error 32 while node_repl instances run.
- Closing the Codex desktop app and terminating ALL processes from `runtimes\cua_node` (0 remaining) does NOT fix it: the next run
  fails with the same os error 32. The same error recurs after all observed cua_node processes are terminated. The process causing the sharing violation has not been identified.
- The log sometimes shows two `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` spawns within milliseconds, and "read ACL helper already running; skipping".
  Inference (unverified): a concurrent sandbox helper (second refresh or the read-ACL helper) holds node_repl.exe while the refresh
  opens it for the root-only ACL update.
- Not determined: which process holds the handle (would need Process Monitor/handle.exe).

## Workaround
Per run: `codex exec ... -c 'windows.sandbox="unelevated"'` — commands and file writes work; config.toml unchanged.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Windows, Codex app installed, config `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`, CLI auto-updated to 0.162.0-alpha.2.
2. In a trusted git repo: `echo "Run Get-Location" | codex exec -C <repo> -s workspace-write -`.
3. Observe the error above; see the sandbox log.

New chats in the Codex page are blocked by the following banner across projects:

> 无法加载工作空间设置
> 请重试以继续聊天

routePattern=/settings/user status=403 errorCode=cloudflare_challenge
routePattern=/accounts/check/{version} status=403 errorCode=cloudflare_challenge

There is an additional timing-dependent behavior: after clicking **Retry**, sending a message while the retry is still loading can establish a chat. This was observed by the affected user; it has not been independently reproduced through automation. Creating a chat through this timing window does not establish that the workspace settings request succeeded.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the Windows desktop app and select the Codex page.
2. Start a new chat in a project. The workspace settings error appears and blocks ordinary sending.
3. Click **Retry** and wait for it to finish. The error persists.
4. Click **Retry** again and send a message while the retry is still loading. The user reports that a chat can be established during this interval.

### What is the expected behavior?

New chats should load workspace settings successfully and allow messages to be sent normally. During a retry, message submission should consistently reflect the current workspace policy state, with a clear supported recovery flow when a settings/account request receives a Cloudflare challenge.

Observed on October 9, 2026:

- Changing proxy nodes, restarting the app, and signing out/in did not resolve the issue.
- Normal access to ChatGPT through the in-app browser completed its automatic check and loaded successfully. The user completed sign-in with the same account.

- The computer restart did not provide sustained recovery.
- `codex doctor` confirmed that configuration parsing and desktop app-server initialization succeed. These checks do not verify successful loading of the renderer's workspace policy.

Related: #51691, which reports recovery after normal browser access, native account refresh, and Retry. In this case, that recovery was not sustained, and the Retry-loading message submission window is an additional observation.

items.body:
## Summary

When the TUI finds a reachable shared app-server with incompatible feature flags, it can disable **Restart with these settings** with:

```text
This server is not managed by Codex.
```

This message is misleading. The condition checked is whether the **Codex app-server daemon manager recognizes the running backend**, not whether the server was launched by a Codex client. Codex Desktop/CLI can launch an app-server that is not owned by that particular daemon manager. The message sounds like the user has started an external server and does not explain what prevents a restart or how to recover safely.

This issue focuses on the **TUI diagnostic and recovery choices**. It does not propose adopting or force-restarting a process without established ownership.

## Observed behavior

In the shared-server feature-mismatch case reported on Linux with Codex CLI 0.161.0 (see #52085), starting plain `codex` showed:

```text
Background server has incompatible feature settings
This session requires api_key_model_discovery to be enabled

Restart will use these shared feature settings:
  api_key_model_discovery = true
  auth_elicitation = true
  code_mode_host = true
  mcp_oauth_refresh_coordination = false
```

The **Restart with these settings** choice was disabled with `This server is not managed by Codex.`, leaving **Run without daemon this time** and **Cancel**.

The user had not manually started an external app-server and was using Codex clients. The precise process launch path/ownership on that host was not independently captured, so this report does **not** assert an incorrect ownership classification.

A non-disruptive recovery **was** confirmed: `codex --disable api_key_model_discovery` (or persisting `[features] api_key_model_discovery = false` in `~/.codex/config.toml`) allowed plain `codex` to attach to the *existing* server, with ChatGPT authentication, without restarting the server or interrupting other work. That option was not disclosed in the TUI.

## Code path

The wording is directly traceable to:

1. [`app-server-daemon/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/47b80571f0d6587060a580c47f6af0cfaefb0d5c/codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/lib.rs#L409-L427): an app-server can answer the socket probe while `running_backend(&settings)` returns `None`.
2. [`tui/src/startup_orchestration.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/47b80571f0d6587060a580c47f6af0cfaefb0d5c/codex-rs/tui/src/startup_orchestration.rs#L542-L573): `managed_daemon = output.backend.is_some()`.
3. [`tui/src/daemon_recovery.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/47b80571f0d6587060a580c47f6af0cfaefb0d5c/codex-rs/tui/src/daemon_recovery.rs#L159-L170): the disabled restart choice translates `!managed_daemon` to `"This server is not managed by Codex."`.

As a result, the UI turns a narrowly defined daemon-management check into a broad statement about “Codex” without disclosing the actual failed criterion.

## Expected behavior

- Use precise terminology, for example: **“The app-server is reachable, but the Codex app-server daemon manager does not recognize it as a managed instance. Automatic restart is unavailable.”**
- Distinguish **server reachability**, **daemon-managed lifecycle ownership**, and **who originally launched the server**. Do not imply a proven launch origin where none was established.
- When the incompatibility is an optional feature flag, show a non-disruptive client-side alternative where applicable (for this case, `codex --disable api_key_model_discovery`), including that it keeps using the existing shared server. Do not present `--no-daemon` as the only non-restart option.
- If useful, point to a read-only daemon-status check and the specific missing management evidence. Continue to refuse potentially disruptive restarts of unowned processes.

## Related, but separate

- #52085 / #51891: feature-default mismatch involving `api_key_model_discovery`.
- #49612: Desktop SSH process/lifecycle ambiguity and unclear recovery.
- #37893: a reachable app-server becoming unmanaged after daemon state loss.
- #24542: Codex Desktop remote proxy starting an app-server outside the managed-daemon lifecycle.

These concern feature compatibility or process lifecycle. This report is specifically about the **misleading TUI diagnosis and absent safe recovery guidance**, which also applies when unmanaged process status is intentional.

### Summary

In the ChatGPT/Codex Windows app, formatted response UI sometimes disappears and the underlying markup is shown as plain text instead.

The same response can render normally with cards/buttons/status elements, but in the Windows app it may instead display raw tags such as:

```text
<row align="center" gap={2}>
<icon name="pause-circle" color="danger" size="lg"/>
<box flex="1" gap={1}>
<text color="secondary" size="xs">...</text>
<button block ...>...</button>
</box>
</row>
```

This appears to be an intermittent client-side rendering issue rather than the model intentionally returning markup.

### What I observed

A response containing a status card and action buttons rendered correctly in one client/view, but the Windows app later showed the component markup literally in the conversation.

Examples of elements that became visible as raw text:

- `<row>`
- `<icon>`
- `<box>`
- `<text>`
- `<button>`
- event-handler-like content such as `onClick={() => GenUI.issueNewTurn(...)}`

The formatted card/button UI was no longer rendered.

### Expected behavior

The Windows app should consistently render supported rich-response / GenUI components as the intended formatted UI.

If a component cannot be rendered, the client should fall back to readable plain text rather than exposing internal component markup or event-handler syntax.

### Actual behavior

The formatting occasionally disappears and the raw component representation is displayed directly in the chat.

### Reproduction

This is intermittent, but the observed flow is roughly:

1. Use ChatGPT/Codex on Windows.
2. Continue a conversation that contains a response with rich UI/status cards/action buttons.
3. Return to the conversation, refresh/reopen it, or continue chatting.
4. In some cases, a previously formatted section is displayed as raw markup instead of the UI.

I have also observed the correctly rendered version of the same content, which makes the difference very obvious.

### Environment

- Platform: Windows desktop app
- Product: ChatGPT / Codex Windows experience
- Date observed: October 9, 2026
- Frequency: Intermittent

### Additional notes

This is especially confusing because the markup includes implementation-looking details such as component names and click handlers. It also makes the response difficult to read and can make action controls unusable.

I can provide the before/after screenshots showing:
1. the broken raw-markup rendering, and
2. the correctly rendered card/button version,
if needed.
